display.title: How Long Ago Was Matan Torah? A Calculator Lesson Before Shavuos
display.summary_short: Using a calculator, Uncle Yossi works out that the Torah was given 3,298 years ago, and counts down the last days of the Omer to Shavuos.
display.summary_long: A pre-Shavuos talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, recorded on Gimmel Sivan 5746. The Torah was given in the year 2448 from creation. Remembering last week's Lag BaOmer calculator lesson, Uncle Yossi has children take out their calculators again: clear the screen, enter 5746, the current year, press the minus key (which looks like a patach), subtract 2448 and press total. The answer: Matan Torah took place 3,298 years ago, and Jews everywhere have celebrated it with joy ever since. Because the people were so eager to receive the Torah, they counted 49 days until the sixth of Sivan, which is why we count the Omer. Today is the third of Sivan, tonight is the 48th day, Wednesday night the 49th, and Thursday is Erev Shavuos, when we welcome the holiday with joy.
display.lesson: The Torah we celebrate on Shavuos is the same Torah given thousands of years ago; welcome it with joy.
